basics.name: Md Monirul Islam
basics.label: R&D Engineer & Team Lead — Cybernetics Hi-Tech Solutions
basics.summary: Robotics R&D engineer working at the intersection of motion control, autonomous systems, and embedded hardware. R&D Engineer & Team Lead at [Cybernetics Hi-Tech Solutions](https://cyberneticsbd.com), Dhaka. Designed and field-deployed a production 3-robot AGV fleet in a live garment factory, a ROS 2 / MoveIt 2 manipulator stack with a custom closed-form 7-DOF IK solver, and contributed to the Jontro Soinik EOD ROV family (v1 and v2) now in UN Peacekeeping service. B.Sc. in EEE from BUET (CGPA 3.85/4.00, ranked 25 of 189, awarded with Honours). **Seeking PhD positions for Fall 2027** in robotics, motion control, or autonomous systems.

work.name: Cybernetics Hi-Tech Solutions (Pvt) Ltd
work.summary: End-to-end design, development, and production deployment of robotic platforms across mobile manipulation, multi-robot autonomy, EOD ROVs, drones, and industrial manufacturing.
highlights: Led design and production deployment of a **3-robot AGV fleet** at The Urmi Group (live RMG facility) — ROS 2, custom EKF with AprilTag fiducial fusion, distributed reservation-based path planning, FleetCore coordinator, 3-layer safety architecture. First-ever AGV solution deployed in Bangladesh.

Built a **ROS 2 / MoveIt 2 mobile manipulator control stack** for an 11-joint tracked platform (7-DOF arm + 2-DOF anti-flipper arm + differential-drive base) — custom closed-form 7-DOF analytical IK replacing KDL, singularity-aware smooth scaling, FK-anchored accumulator, MoveIt-planned special commands (return-to-rest, named configs) with per-tick collision validity across arm / anti-flipper / carrier, 5-state FSM. Hardware assembly underway; once field-tested, set for UN peacekeeping deployment.

Contributed to the **Jontro Soinik EOD ROV family (v1 and v2)** — S-curve arm motion profile (v1), custom multi-drop bus replacing the v1 star topology (v2), differential-drive speed synchronization (v2), BLDC motor synchronization, RS-485 inter-node communication, custom PCB design (Altium / KiCad), 48 V power distribution. v1 deployed in UN Peacekeeping Mission, Mali (2024); v2 set for the Republic of Congo (2025).

Designed **SD15-N autonomous target-tracking surveillance drone** — YOLOv11n on Raspberry Pi 5 + Pixhawk 2.4.8, real-time bounding-box-to-velocity-command pipeline over MAVLink. 1,000 ft altitude, 15 km range, 20 m/s.

Designed a **50 kg heavy-lift multirotor** — 30 min flight, 15 km comms range, 1.5:1 thrust-to-weight ratio. Custom BMS, propulsion sizing, structural frame analysis. The battery + motor sizing study is published as an interactive in-browser **Drone Battery Optimizer** on the portfolio site.
Designed and manufactured the **CyberMaker Titan550 Pro industrial 3D printer** — CoreXY motion system, 510 × 510 × 550 mm build volume, ±0.02 mm repeatability, Marlin 2.0 firmware.
Delivered the **maiden flight of a VTOL quad-plane prototype** for heavy-lift and long-endurance applications.
Lead engineer mentoring a small team of R&D engineers; ownership of system architecture, hardware selection, software development, field commissioning, and production handover.

publications.name: Peer-Aware Distributed Path Planning for a Production-Deployed Multi-AGV Fleet in a Human-Occupied Garment Factory
publications.title: Peer-Aware Distributed Path Planning for a Production-Deployed Multi-AGV Fleet in a Human-Occupied Garment Factory
publications.summary: Decentralized A* path-planning and coordination scheme deployed on a 3-robot AGV fleet running inside a live garment factory alongside hundreds of workers with no physical separation. Each robot publishes its plan as timestamped grid waypoints; peers treat them as spatiotemporal reservations with three conflict checks (node / edge-swap / final-cell). Continuous timestamp maintenance keeps ETAs honest between replans, and obstacles are handled without dropping the active plan. Months of zero-collision production operation; case study reports protocol + throughput / recovery measurements. *Corresponding author; manuscript in preparation.*

publications.name: Experimental Speed Synchronization of a Dual-BLDC Tracked Differential-Drive Vehicle Using a GA-Tuned Bilateral Cross-Coupled Controller on a Dual-MCU Architecture
publications.title: Experimental Speed Synchronization of a Dual-BLDC Tracked Differential-Drive Vehicle Using a GA-Tuned Bilateral Cross-Coupled Controller on a Dual-MCU Architecture
publications.summary: Distributed dual-MCU implementation of bilateral cross-coupled speed synchronization for a tracked differential-drive vehicle driven by two deliberately mismatched 3-phase BLDC motors. Each motor regulated by its own MCU running a PID loop with velocity/acceleration feedforward; a bilateral cross-coupled term, evaluated identically on both nodes from a dedicated 1 ms inter-MCU speed exchange, drives the inter-motor speed difference toward zero. All gains GA-tuned offline. Reduces peak transient inter-motor speed error by 79 %, RMS by 73 %, accumulated straight-line heading drift by 80 % vs an independent-PID baseline. *Corresponding author; draft linked above.*
